School

Analytic Philosophy quotes

Analytic philosophy emphasizes argumentative clarity, logical analysis, and careful attention to language—without reducing to a single doctrine.

28 passages · 4 voices in this archive selection

Overview

From early logic and ordinary-language debates to ethics of intention and virtue (Anscombe, Foot) and philosophy of language (Wittgenstein), analytic work in this archive favors precise distinctions over rhetorical flourish.

Historical notes

Twentieth-century analytic philosophy grows from Frege, Russell, Moore, and the Vienna Circle into postwar Oxford and contemporary ethics, mind, and language.

Core ideas

  • Clarify concepts before building systems.
  • Language and logic shape what can be said truly.
  • Moral philosophy can be rigorous without ignoring practice.
  • Intention and action repay careful description.

Thinkers in this archive

Ludwig Wittgenstein , Bertrand Russell , Elizabeth Anscombe , Philippa Foot

FAQ

What is analytic philosophy?

It is a family of approaches valuing clarity, argument, and analysis of language and concepts—especially in the English-speaking tradition.

Is analytic philosophy only about language?

No. Language is a method and topic, but analytic work also covers mind, ethics, metaphysics, and science.
